records.supported_name_scope: Thlewiaza River is supported for the principal Nueltin–Edehon–Ranger Seal–Hudson Bay corridor. It is not accepted as the representative identity of all five modeled fragments: the northern attachment includes the separately mapped Kognak and Tha-anne corridors, followed by a modeled southward link toward the Thlewiaza that the inspected official mapping does not establish as one through-river. Western feeder and lake-passage names are not extended from the principal river label.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Northern Canada: a western headwater extension at the northeastern Saskatchewan–northwestern Manitoba border, the Snyder/Kasmere lake-chain setting and Nueltin Lake, then the Thlewiaza corridor east across southern Nunavut to Hudson Bay south of Arviat. The additional northern branch lies in the Gregoire/Boland/Hicks–Elliott lake-chain setting and the Kognak–Tha-anne corridor south of the Henik lakes. The adjacent Tha-anne and McConnell coastal drainages must not be collapsed into the Thlewiaza merely because the modeled collection is connected.
records.completion_scope: Completed geographical and naming-scope assessment of the complete selected geometry, including all three modeled mainstem pieces and both northern pieces. The full-feature review flag means all pieces and their scope limits were assessed, not that every modeled vertex has a matched named natural channel. Sufficient readable official evidence establishes the group scope hold now; it is not an access or source-acquisition backlog. A future naming or geometry decision would need to address the northern cross-drainage attachment and western feeder scope before applying one group label.

naming_scope_details.principal_supported_corridor: Thlewiaza River, bounded to the Nueltin outlet and downstream Edehon–Ranger Seal–Hudson Bay corridor, with the Manitoba Nueltin drainage supported at system level.

separately_supported_northern_corridors.role: Named northern receiving/continuing corridor on sheets 65H/65A; not a Thlewiaza alias.

records.supported_name_scope: Río Negro is supported as the representative identity of this drainage collection, with Uruguay retained as a geographic qualifier. This does not name every selected fragment Río Negro. The modeled mainstem begins on an eastern feeder in Cerro Largo rather than following the named Negro upstream into Brazil. The collection also includes a northern Cuñapirú–Tacuarembó corridor, a southern Yí corridor and the middle-river reservoir passages. Exact local headwater names, transition vertices and reservoir-channel names are not assigned.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual selected course was followed from its east-to-west feeder south of Aceguá into the southwesterly Negro corridor, past the northern Tacuarembó approach, through the central reservoir succession and lower western bends to the Río Uruguay. The separate long northern branch and southern Yí approach were also inspected. This is the Río Negro of the Uruguay–Río de la Plata drainage, not an unqualified name transfer based on a bounding box or model membership.
records.region: Uruguay's Río Negro drainage, from the Cerro Largo upper-feeder setting through central Uruguay to the Río Uruguay outlet, with a northern branch reaching the Rivera border vicinity. The wider natural basin also extends into Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
records.completion_scope: Completed representative-system correspondence for all four modeled-mainstem pieces and both tributary chains. Several optional map requests were unavailable, but the acquired original maps and direct official text are sufficient for this bounded finding. No further source acquisition is pending. Individual reach naming would be separate work and remains unapplied.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Uruguay; the river drains to Río Uruguay and its wider basin is transboundary with Brazil. The parenthetical qualifier is editorial disambiguation, not a claim that official sources print it as part of the name.
naming_scope_details.unassigned: Eastern Cerro Largo feeder name; the northernmost short feeder pieces; exact river-name/confluence transitions; exact reservoir entry/exit vertices; local lower-mouth channel name.
naming_scope_details.excluded_name_transfer: The named Negro headwater route in Brazil is not substituted for the selected eastern feeder. Tacuarembó Grande, Tacuarembó Chico and the neighboring Yaguarí/Caraguatá branches are not transferred wholesale to the selected northern chain. Reservoir names are preserved as waterbody context rather than blanket river aliases.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The cached line and its modeled mainstem classification establish the selected object to inspect, not a hydronym, a current-flow observation, a survey of channel permanence or exact named-river length.

records.supported_name_scope: Rio Pardo is supported as the representative identity of this drainage collection in northern Minas Gerais and southern Bahia. The central and downstream selected corridor corresponds to the mapped Pardo through Rio Pardo de Minas, the Machado Mineiro corridor, Cândido Sales, Itambé, the Potiraguá–Mascote corridor and Canavieiras. The western northernmost modeled headwater is not the source point specified by ANA, and no uniform reach name, exact name-transition vertex or natural-river length is assigned to the complete modeled line.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Atlantic-draining Rio Pardo of northern Minas Gerais and southern Bahia, Brazil, ending in the Canavieiras coastal setting. Retain the Minas Gerais–Bahia qualifier because Pardo is a repeated river name. This is not the Pardo of the Rio Grande drainage in Minas Gerais–São Paulo or the Pardo of the Guaíba drainage in Rio Grande do Sul.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system identity. Readable independent official cartography and direct official text cover the selected route and establish its scope. The unresolved local designation of the initial headwater is preserved as a reach-naming limit, not an unfinished acquisition or a reason to force a single name over all geometry.

naming_scope_details.display_disambiguator: Minas Gerais–Bahia is a geographic qualifier added to distinguish the repeated name, not a claim that the qualifier is part of the official river name.
naming_scope_details.upstream_limit: The northernmost modeled starting approach and ANA’s specified source point are not identical. No headwater synonym or name-change point is established for that complete initial approach.
naming_scope_details.waterbody_and_branch_limit: Representative-system identity does not make every feeder, reservoir passage, tributary or estuarine channel Rio Pardo. Only one mainstem fragment is present in the selected cached collection; no additional tributary fragments are named.
naming_scope_details.model_limit: No assertion of exact survey-level alignment, current discharge, present reservoir operation, official total river length or contemporary shoreline follows from this correspondence.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river name is established for this complete modeled MAIN_RIV path across the western Inland Ice. This is a completed feature-class and naming-scope hold, not proof that every marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Western Greenland Inland Ice, from the interior west/northwest of the Summit sector toward the western ice margin in the broad coastal sector south of Upernavik Isfjord and north of Rink Isbræ/Karrat Isfjord. Those geographical labels are context only, not assigned river or terminal-glacier names.
records.completion_scope: Complete selected-path scope assessment. A future river-name assignment would require positive natural-feature identity evidence; no further acquisition is required now to establish the hold.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
